# Tensile-test elastic modulus estimates

A straight-line least-squares fit, stress = E × strain + intercept, was applied to all measured points for each material. The fitted slope is the elastic modulus. Fits use the full recorded strain range (0.0002–0.0020); this estimates the modulus over that range and assumes the supplied points are in the linear elastic regime.

![Stress-strain data with material-level linear fits](results/elastic_modulus.png)

| Material | Modulus (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² | Specimens | Points | Mean specimen modulus ± SD (GPa) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| aluminum | 69.38 | -0.31 | 0.99834 | 3 | 30 | 69.38 ± 1.76 |
| steel | 199.06 | 0.62 | 0.99844 | 3 | 30 | 199.06 ± 2.00 |
| titanium | 116.56 | -0.77 | 0.99788 | 3 | 30 | 116.56 ± 1.71 |

The modulus values are the slopes of pooled material-level fits. The final column summarizes slopes from separate fits to each specimen and shows their between-specimen spread (sample standard deviation). The fitted intercept is retained rather than forced through the origin.

item.text:
The Calkit analysis is set up and the pipeline ran successfully. It fits a line to all recorded points for each material, keeping the intercept free.

| Material | Estimated modulus | R² | Specimens |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Aluminum | 69.38 GPa | 0.99834 | 3 |
| Steel | 199.06 GPa | 0.99844 | 3 |
| Titanium | 116.56 GPa | 0.99788 | 3 |

The short write-up includes the fit details and between-specimen spread: [results.md](/private/tmp/tmp5my_f_p0/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/results.md). The figure is [elastic_modulus.png](/private/tmp/tmp5my_f_p0/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/results/elastic_modulus.png), and [analyze.py](/private/tmp/tmp5my_f_p0/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/analyze.py) reproduces both outputs through the Calkit pipeline.
